WITH rep_counts AS (
    SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.City, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS customer_count
    FROM Customer AS c
    JOIN Employee AS e
      ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
    GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City
),
city_averages AS (
    SELECT City, AVG(customer_count) AS average_count
    FROM rep_counts
    GROUP BY City
),
above_average AS (
    SELECT r.EmployeeId, r.City, r.customer_count, a.average_count
    FROM rep_counts AS r
    JOIN city_averages AS a
      ON r.City = a.City OR (r.City IS NULL AND a.City IS NULL)
    WHERE r.customer_count > a.average_count
),
all_kept AS (
    SELECT SUM(customer_count) AS total_customers
    FROM above_average
)
SELECT aa.City,
       SUM(aa.customer_count) AS total_customers,
       AVG(aa.customer_count - aa.average_count) AS average_excess,
       AVG(1.0 * aa.customer_count / ak.total_customers) AS average_share
FROM above_average AS aa
CROSS JOIN all_kept AS ak
GROUP BY aa.City;

assumptions.assumption: A rep's city is Employee.City; reps with no customers are excluded because counts are formed from matched customers.
